scope: Catalogued program-ROM data regions used by the translated C gamecore. This is an incremental inventory, not a claim that every byte in program.rom is classified.

status_definitions.extracted: Named C data; byte-for-byte test against the source ROM and replay lockstep evidence.
status_definitions.mapped: Range, reader and purpose are understood, but the gamecore still reads prg_mem.
status_definitions.partial: A stable range or reader is known, but the complete structure needs further analysis.

regions.note: Index bound confirmed against the actual T3310 contents: all entries are multiples of 8 in [0x30, 0xF8], plus (random & 0x06), so the address never leaves 0x3330-0x33FF. IMPORTANT (added after decoding the table's own MSB:LSB payload, not just its own index bound): the 104 MSB:LSB pairs stored in this table resolve to 34 distinct target addresses that are NOT confined to the 18 closed-loop pattern lists at 0x1020-0x13FF -- 18 of the 34 addresses land there, but the other 16 (0x2C00, 0x2C34, 0x2C90, 0x2CC8, 0x2D00, 0x2D44, 0x2D88, 0x2DC0, 0x2E20, 0x2E6C, 0x2E90, 0x2EC4, 0x2F00, 0x2F34, 0x2F64, 0x2FA0) land in a second, physically disjoint 1024-byte pattern-list cluster at 0x2C00-0x2FFF (same 0x00-terminator/0xFF-padding structure, same proven <=0x1F value bound, confirmed by direct byte inspection). Two further addresses in that second cluster (0x2E00, 0x2E40 -- patterns 26 and 28) are reached only via a separate mechanism (alien_logic.c:l3028, the breakout scheduler), not through this table. Any consumer of the address values this table produces (not just this table's own bytes) must account for both clusters -- the alien_movement_update/alien_animation_update reads in alien_logic.c that follow these pointers are now extracted too, as alien-movement-pattern-cluster-a (0x1000-0x13FF) and alien-movement-pattern-cluster-b (0x2C00-0x2FFF), accessed via phoenix_alien_movement_byte().

regions.note: Originally catalogued as two disjoint 32-byte ranges (0x3B60-0x3B7F, 0x3BB0-0x3BCF). l3844_small_bird_hit's index (b+0x60) never dips below 0x3B60 (b in [0,0x4F], so the index stays in [0x3B60,0x3BAF], always inside the T3B60 data table -- confirmed by direct range analysis, no wrap possible there). l38bc_large_hit's index (b+0xB0) does wrap below 0x60 for b in [0x50,0x6F] (tile in [0xE0,0xFF], grown-bird tiles), landing in the code bytes preceding T3B60 (0x3B00-0x3B5F). This is not a theoretical edge case: instrumented at collision_detection.c:l38bc_large_hit and run against bird-investigation.txt (13935 frames), the wrap fired 27 times across 12 distinct tile values (e.g. tile=0xE3 -> index 0x03, tile=0xE8 -> index 0x08, tile=0xF9 -> index 0x19), landing squarely inside l3b02's function body ($3B02-$3B19) among others. The full page is extracted to preserve that confirmed wrap exactly. Those code bytes (0x3B00-0x3B5F) are not unclassified: they are the opcodes for l3b02/l3b1b/l3b28/l3b33/l3b43, already translated as ordinary functions in sound_dispatcher.c and called there as code. phoenix_bird_hitmask_page is a deliberate byte-for-byte duplicate of the same physical ROM bytes for their separate, unrelated use as inert lookup data on this wrap path -- a compiled C function's object bytes bear no relation to the original Z80 opcodes, so only this literal copy is valid for the data-read use; it must not be derived from or merged with the sound_dispatcher.c translation.
regions.evidence: test_phoenix_tables.py plus byte-identical pre/post-extraction RAM dump over 13935 scripted frames (bird-investigation.txt, exercises grown-bird/large-hit tile IDs); wrap occurrence independently confirmed via temporary instrumentation of l38bc_large_hit (27 hits, 12 distinct tile values, removed after verification).

regions.note: Previously uncatalogued (was in dynamic_or_payload_readers as 'alien movement lists'). Read via a RAM-stored 16-bit pointer ($4B50-$4B6F, M4394:M4395) whose value is proven to always land in this range or in alien-movement-pattern-cluster-b: enumerated every writer (phoenix_alien_layout_pointers' constant 0x1000 initial value, phoenix_alien_closed_loop_pointers' 34 decoded target addresses -- 18 of them here -- and l3028's breakout targets, both in cluster B). The pointer's low byte free-wheels within a fixed 256-byte page (0xFF+1 wraps to 0x00) so any reachable address stays inside this array; accessed via phoenix_alien_movement_byte() which also selects cluster A vs B. All non-0xFF bytes confirmed <= 0x1F by direct inspection, matching the index domain of phoenix_alien_direction_vectors/phoenix_alien_shape_offset_page.

regions.asm: T1500/T1520 plus an unlabelled level-position table from 0x1540
regions.note: Previously uncatalogued (flagged only as a caveat in alien-control-state-pointers' note). init_alien_positions does '0x1500 | lsb' with lsb read from a 16-entry pointer table (0x063A-0x0649, see alien-position-pointer-table below); real (non-0xFF) lsb values are 0x40,0x60,0x80,0xA0,0xC0,0xE0, and the read window is up to 32 bytes (AliensLeft capped at 16), so the worst real case (lsb=0xE0) reaches exactly 0x15FF -- never spilling into phoenix_alien_shape_offset_page (0x1600+). Slots 6,7,14,15 of the pointer table hold 0xFF placeholders that would overflow past 0x15FF if ever selected; empirically confirmed (via temporary instrumentation, removed after verification) never to occur while AliensLeft > 0 across four long, varied scripts. The full 0x1500-0x15FF page is extracted rather than a narrower slice to keep that safety margin explicit; it deliberately overlaps alien-control-state-pointers (0x1500-0x151F) and alien-initial-layout-pointers (0x1520-0x153F) -- same literal ROM bytes, independently verified, kept as separate arrays because this read site's own reachable range needs the page.
regions.evidence: test_phoenix_tables.py plus byte-identical pre/post-extraction RAM dumps over 3610 passive frames, 4600 scripted frames (extended_playthrough.txt), 13300 scripted frames (my_session.txt) and 13935 scripted frames (bird-investigation.txt). Coverage of the actual index/lsb values reached was confirmed via temporary instrumentation across those four scripts plus two_player_last_grown_bird.txt (13253 frames): only indices {0,1,4,5,8,9} were observed, all mapping to real lsb values with maxAddr never exceeding 0x15FF; the 0xFF sentinel slots (6,7,14,15) were never selected.

regions.note: Two reads (a scrolling-text character lookup and a DE screen-address pointer pair), both indexed via Counter98, a free-running 16-bit counter -- not mathematically bounded like the other extracted tables. Bound established empirically via temporary hit-counting instrumentation on passive (input-less) runs of 3610, 30000 and 60000 frames: the reached address never exceeded 0x1B3F across all three lengths (2808 and 5543 calls respectively at the longer runs, same ceiling both times). Extracted to 0x1B5F (0x1B60 exclusive) as a safety margin beyond the observed maximum; the tail bytes duplicate the start of mothership-and-player-explosion-pointers (0x1B40+) -- same physical ROM bytes, kept separate because this read site's own reachable range needs the margin. Also serves print_text_lines()'s 0x1960/0x19C0/0x1A00 call sites (see attract-text-page/players-button-text and phoenix_text_byte() for the shared dispatch), previously bypassing this array via mem_read until the mem_read audit found and fixed that.

known_issues.note: RESOLVED (21 July 2026). Two independent C translations of the same ASM routine (InitGlobalLevelData, $0580-$0595) existed: a `static` one in state_init.c using its own local T0598/T05A8/T05B4/T05C0/T05CC arrays (called from state_2_init_game_and_level_data), and the external one in init_global_level_data.c using level-data-pointer-table/level-data-page above (called from attract_mode.c's demo dispatch). Both were genuinely live and held identical ROM bytes. Fixed by deleting state_init.c's static duplicate (function body and its 5 local arrays) and having it call the shared external init_global_level_data() instead, same as attract_mode.c already did.
